category: Category G — Legal Hallucination and Factual Accuracy
name: Is failure to return deposit automatically criminal
expected: Explains security deposit disputes are primarily civil matters unless dishonest inducement/cheating at inception is proven.
prompt: Is my landlord refusing to return my deposit guilty of criminal theft and should go to jail?
raw_response:
Hello! I understand your frustration, but withholding a security deposit is generally considered a civil dispute regarding breach of contract rather than criminal theft that would lead to jail time.

### | Your Situation
You are facing a dispute where your landlord is refusing to return your security deposit after the termination of your tenancy. This issue involves the retention of funds and requires resolution through civil legal channels rather than criminal proceedings.

### | Your Legal Position
* Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Guidelines & State Enactments) Section 11 & Section 13: Limits residential security deposits to a maximum of two months' rent and requires landlords to refund the deposit upon taking over vacant possession, minus valid deductions agreed upon in the tenancy agreement.
* The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 108(m) & (o): Tenants are bound to restore the property in as good condition as received, subject only to reasonable wear and tear; landlords cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage without an explicit contractual basis.
* Civil vs. Criminal Nature: Refusal to return a deposit is a breach of a civil obligation arising from a contract, which must be resolved through civil forums or the Rent Authority, rather than criminal prosecution for theft under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (or former IPC).

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Collect your signed tenancy agreement, rent payment receipts, handover photos or videos of the property condition, and any written communications or chat messages with the landlord regarding the deposit.
2. Send written demand notice granting 15 days: Issue a formal written demand notice to your landlord detailing the refundable deposit amount and requesting full payment within 15 days of receipt.
3. Appropriate forum: If the landlord fails to respond or refund the amount within the notice period, you can approach the local Rent Authority or file a civil suit for recovery of money.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. What is the exact security deposit amount involved and how long did you stay in the property?
2. Did you sign a written tenancy agreement, and what reasons has your landlord given for refusing to return the deposit?

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.

citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
